lesson.scenario: A three-node Raft group elects one leader, replicates a command, and fences a stale leader by term and log consistency.

steps.title: Start a new election term
steps.narration: After randomized timeout, A increments and persists currentTerm=12, votes for itself, and requests votes with its last log metadata.

steps.outcome: Every node grants at most one vote in term 12.
steps.invariant: Terms and votes are persisted, votes require an up-to-date candidate log, followers accept entries only after matching the previous index and term, and a leader advances commit for a current-term entry only after majority replication.

steps.title: Win with an up-to-date log
steps.narration: B and C grant A because its log is at least as up to date as theirs; two votes already form a majority of three.

steps.title: Append a term-owned entry
steps.narration: A appends locally, then sends AppendEntries with prevLogIndex=88 and prevLogTerm=11; B persists index 89 and acknowledges.

steps.outcome: The command is stored on a majority but not yet applied.
steps.invariant: Terms and votes are persisted, votes require an up-to-date candidate log, followers accept entries only after matching the previous index and term, and a leader advances commit for a current-term entry only after majority replication.

steps.title: Commit the current-term entry
steps.narration: A sees index 89 from its current term on A and B, advances commitIndex, and includes 89 in subsequent heartbeats.
steps.outcome: The command is durably committed by quorum.
steps.invariant: Terms and votes are persisted, votes require an up-to-date candidate log, followers accept entries only after matching the previous index and term, and a leader advances commit for a current-term entry only after majority replication.

steps.title: Apply once and reject stale leadership
steps.narration: All caught-up nodes apply index 89 in order; an isolated former leader at term 11 steps down when its AppendEntries is rejected with currentTerm=12.
steps.outcome: Clients observe one committed state-machine transition and stale leaders cannot commit.
steps.invariant: Terms and votes are persisted, votes require an up-to-date candidate log, followers accept entries only after matching the previous index and term, and a leader advances commit for a current-term entry only after majority replication.

production.scenario: A managed Kubernetes control plane needs a single ordered history of object changes before schedulers and controllers act on them.
components: kubectl users and control-plane components issuing object changes from many regions
service boundary that authenticates callers and validates object schemas
control-plane service that uses Raft to elect one leader and order control-plane mutations
durable authority for cluster objects, revisions, and watch history
consume committed object watches and drive pods, services, and repair loops
control path that replaces failed voters, restores snapshots, and gates failover
observability path for election churn, commit lag, and quorum headroom
flows: Users and controllers send writes that must become part of one ordered control-plane history.
The API server forwards validated mutations into the Raft-backed ordering path.
The consensus module advances the committed revision in the authoritative etcd store.
Schedulers and controllers react only to committed object revisions from durable state.
Recovery control manages voter replacement and snapshot seeding after failures.
The state store exposes snapshots and log position needed for safe recovery workflows.
Operations dashboards track leader changes, append latency, and quorum margin.
